_comment: Liveness and readiness probes for the Container Apps that shipped without any.
Five of eight apps had an empty `probes` array, so Container Apps had no way
to tell a hung process from a healthy one: a worker whose event loop had
stopped turning kept its replica, kept its lease on the queue, and reported
the revision Healthy. Only qdrant-cc, fastapi-cc and laravel-octane-cc were
covered, and those three are the ones nobody worries about.
Applied by apply-probes.sh, which merges these into each app's live template
rather than replacing it. Keep this file and the live config in step: CD only
ever sends `--image`, so probes set here survive every deploy, which also
means a drift introduced here is permanent until someone notices.
TIMING. failureThreshold x periodSeconds is how long a wedged container
keeps running. Liveness is deliberately slack (>= 90s) because the cost of a
false restart is a killed job; readiness is tight because its only cost is a

redis-cc._why: TCP 6379, no HTTP surface. A tcpSocket probe proves the listener accepts connections, which is the failure that matters: Redis wedged on a slow AOF rewrite stops accepting long before the process exits.

hatchet-cc._why: The engine speaks gRPC on 7077 and nothing else on this app's ingress. Container Apps probes cannot speak gRPC, so tcpSocket is the honest ceiling here -- it catches a dead or unbound listener, not a broken engine. initialDelay is 45s because the engine runs its own schema migration on boot.

hatchet-worker-cc._why: The Hatchet Python SDK ships a healthcheck server that answers /health on 8001 and returns 503 when the action listener's event loop has been blocked past a threshold. That is exactly the audit's finding -- a hung worker staying in rotation -- so this app gets a real health signal rather than a socket check. The env block below turns it on; without it the port is closed and every probe fails.

env._why: The SDK default is 5s, which a CPU-bound stretch inside the listener process would trip routinely. Parsing runs in a process pool, so the listener should never block for 30s; if it does, it is wedged.
env.name: HATCHET_CLIENT_WORKER_HEALTHCHECK_EVENT_LOOP_BLOCK_THRESHOLD_SECONDS

laravel-reverb-cc._why: Reverb registers its own health route at /up (Servers/Reverb/Http/Factory.php), served by the same event loop that serves websockets -- so a 200 there means the loop is turning, which a tcpSocket check on 8080 would not.

laravel-horizon-cc._why: `php artisan horizon` serves no HTTP, and Container Apps probes speak only HTTP and TCP -- there is no exec probe to run `horizon:status` with. So the image now starts a small health listener alongside the supervisor (docker/horizon-entrypoint.sh -> docker/horizon-health.php) that answers /up on 8080 by reading Horizon's own master-supervisor heartbeat out of Redis. A stale heartbeat is the wedged-supervisor signal; the listener answering at all is not. Liveness reads /up and readiness reads /ready because they must disagree about `horizon:pause`: a paused supervisor is not ready, but restarting it would silently undo a deliberate operator action.
laravel-horizon-cc._requires: laravel image built at or after the commit that adds docker/horizon-entrypoint.sh, AND the app's command set to that entrypoint. apply-probes.sh checks both and skips this app rather than configuring a probe that can only fail.
